 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 06.03.2013, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khanapur, in MVC No.2418/2010, on the ground that quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal is exorbitant and prays to reduce the quantum of compensation.

2. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
3.
The factum of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident, coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.

4. The tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings.
50,000  NC: 2023:KHC-D:12398  2. Loss of happiness and future 1,00,000  amenities.
3. Loss of income during the 20,000  treatment period.

sentences.text: Incidental charges.

3,000  6. Loss of future income.
Future medical expenses.
In the present case from the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant has sustained fracture of lateral condyle of tibia and fracture of neck of fibula of right leg.
The claimant is a carpenter by profession.
The doctor had assessed the physical disability at 35% to the particular limb.
The same is taken by the tribunal towards whole body.
Taking 35% of physical disability to the whole body is excessive one.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and the nature of profession of the claimant, it is just and proper to take 12% as functional disability.
The accident is caused on 10.01.2010.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income would be Rs.5,500/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service NC: 2023:KHC-D:12398 Authority.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Service NC: 2023:KHC-D:12398 Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The claimant was aged 28 years old at the time of accident.
Therefore the appropriate applicable multiplier is 17.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is hereby re-assessed and quantified as Rs.1,34,640/- (Rs.5,500 x 12% x 12 x 17).
6. Further the compensation awarded under other heads is also found to be on higher side.
Hence the same is required to be modified.
Therefore, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, a compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards injuries pain and suffering, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities are awarded.

Further, a compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards medical expenses,
Rs.15,000/- towards incidental expenses like food, nourishment, travelling, attendant charges, etc.,
and Rs.16,500/- towards loss of income during laid up and treatment period for a period of three months, is awarded.
Further, a compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.

Thus the claimant would be entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards injuries, pain and 50,000  suffering.
 2. Towards medical expenses.
5,000  3. Towards loss of amenities.

 5. Towards incidental charges like 15,000  attendant charges, food,
nourishment, conveyance, etc.,.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,66,140/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.5,64,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
9. There may be 7-8 persons were travelling in the maxi cab.
But only one claim petition is filed.
Therefore, NC: 2023:KHC-D:12398 the insurance company shall pay the compensation.
The tribunal is correct in fastening liability on the insurance company.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

10. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal filed by the insurance company is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 06.03.2013, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khanapur, in MVC No.2418/2010, stands modified.
iii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,66,140/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.5,64,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:12398 iv) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
v) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
vi) No order as to costs.
vii) Draw award accordingly.

SD/-
